classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate amplitude and horizontal scaling while keeping the requested interval fixed, determining whether it contains a half-wave or two complete cycles and locating the resulting key points.

inlines.text: . Sketch each of the following on the interval

spec.description: Editable equation-driven sine curve; black axes, blue curve, no grid, endpoint circles or curve arrows.

answer.worked: Replacing $y$ with $\frac{y}{2}$ gives a vertical dilation of factor $2$: $(x,y)\mapsto(x,2y)$. On $[-\pi,\pi]$, sketch a smooth sine curve through $(-\pi,0)$, $(-\frac{\pi}{2},-2)$, $(0,0)$, $(\frac{\pi}{2},2)$ and $(\pi,0)$.

spec.description: Complete sine sketch with unchanged horizontal coordinates and doubled vertical coordinates; source answer axes are rendered in house black.

answer.short: Increasing half-wave through $(-\pi,-\tfrac12)$, $(0,0)$ and $(\pi,\tfrac12)$, flattening at both endpoints.
answer.worked: Replacing $x$ with $\frac{x}{2}$ gives a horizontal dilation of factor $2$; multiplying the output by $\frac{1}{2}$ gives a vertical dilation of factor $\frac{1}{2}$. Thus $(x,y)\mapsto(2x,\frac{y}{2})$. On the required interval $[-\pi,\pi]$, the corresponding original inputs are $[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}]$. Sketch the increasing half-wave through $(-\pi,-\frac{1}{2})$, $(0,0)$ and $(\pi,\frac{1}{2})$, flattening at both ends.

spec.description: Increasing half-wave with horizontal tangent at each endpoint; no endpoint circles or curve arrows. House black axes and blue curve.

answer.short: Two cycles on $[-\pi,\pi]$, amplitude $\frac{1}{2}$ and period $\pi$; zeros at $-\pi,-\frac{\pi}{2},0,\frac{\pi}{2},\pi$.
answer.worked: Replacing $x$ with $2x$ gives a horizontal dilation of factor $\frac{1}{2}$; multiplying the output by $\frac{1}{2}$ gives a vertical dilation of factor $\frac{1}{2}$. Thus $(x,y)\mapsto(\frac{x}{2},\frac{y}{2})$. The period is $\pi$. On $[-\pi,\pi]$, sketch two cycles with zeros at $-\pi,-\frac{\pi}{2},0,\frac{\pi}{2},\pi$, maxima at $(-\frac{3\pi}{4},\frac{1}{2})$ and $(\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{1}{2})$, and minima at $(-\frac{\pi}{4},-\frac{1}{2})$ and $(\frac{3\pi}{4},-\frac{1}{2})$.

spec.description: Complete two-cycle sine sketch, retaining source tick placement with positive amplitude left of the vertical axis and negative amplitude right.

answer.short: Increasing half-wave through $(-\pi,-2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(\pi,2)$, flattening at both endpoints.
answer.worked: Replacing $x$ with $\frac{x}{2}$ gives a horizontal dilation of factor $2$; multiplying the output by $2$ gives a vertical dilation of factor $2$. Thus $(x,y)\mapsto(2x,2y)$. On the required interval $[-\pi,\pi]$, the corresponding original inputs are $[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}]$. Sketch the increasing half-wave through $(-\pi,-2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(\pi,2)$, flattening at both ends.

spec.description: Increasing half-wave with horizontal tangent at both endpoints; source negative amplitude label remains right of the vertical axis.
